A_target.statement:
Let $N$ be a [[Definition:Normal Subgroup|normal subgroup]] of a [[Definition:Group|group]] $G$.
Then $H \mapsto H / N$ is an inclusion-preserving [[Definition:Bijection|bijection]] from the subgroups of $G$ containing $N$ to the subgroups of $G / N$, under which normal subgroups correspond.

B_source.statement:
Let $\phi: G \to K$ be a [[Definition:Surjection|surjective]] [[Definition:Group Homomorphism|homomorphism]] with [[Definition:Kernel of Group Homomorphism|kernel]] $N$.
Then images and preimages of subgroups are subgroups, and for $H \le G$:
:$\map {\phi^{-1} } {\map \phi H} = H N$

substitutions.the homomorphism phi: the quotient map q: G -> G/N

derived.H N = H for H containing N: the preimage of the image recovers H

object_map.reformulation: Run the correspondence through the quotient map, whose kernel is exactly the subgroup being collapsed.

validity_conditions: Only subgroups containing N are recovered from their images.
Surjectivity of q gives that the image of a preimage is the original subgroup.
proof_plan: Apply the source result to the quotient map $q: G \to G / N$, whose kernel is $N$.

For $N \le H \le G$, $\map {q^{-1} } {\map q H} = H N = H$.
For $L \le G / N$, $\map q {\map {q^{-1} } L} = L$ by surjectivity, and $\map {q^{-1} } L \supseteq N$.
Both assignments preserve inclusion and are mutually inverse, so they form a bijection.
